_doctrine: FLOW SURFACES AND COLUMN MAPS, DECLARED SO gas-lint CAN HOLD US TO THEM.
meta/FLOW_DOCTRINE.md states thirteen rules for building a Flow in this repo, each with the incident that produced it. Most are not machine-checkable. Two are, and this file is what makes them so.

RULE 7 — two column maps for the same sheet will drift. 34_QueueWatchdog.js:166 records the habit that saved a wrong fix: derive from the writer, verify against the constant. It exists because RQ05 in 05_TeacherIntakePipeline.js had drifted one column out of sync with the queueRow array it describes, so anything reading row[RQ05.STATUS] would have compared a spreadsheet ID against "PENDING_EXTRACTION" forever without erroring. The Central Ledger version of the same drift cost a live session: a shift made LEDGER.TEACHER_EMAIL return a person's name. `columnMaps` below declares every place a sheet's layout is written down twice, and Check H compares them.

RULE 9 — separate the four causes of "nothing happened". Nothing came back is one answer covering four: the Flow was never built, its trigger matches no rows, it writes to the wrong columns, or the model call errored. The third looks exactly like the first, so each cause needs its own check. `flowSurfaces` below declares which functions play those roles for each flow, and Check I verifies they exist in the right project.

SAME NAME IS NOT SAME SHEET. cas-ccps and kos-personal both have a STAGING_PIPELINE, and they are different sheets with different widths (6 vs 7 columns) in different spreadsheets. That is why groups are declared explicitly rather than inferred from a tab name -- an inferring check would compare the two and report a false conflict every run, which is how a check gets muted.
A GROUP WITH ONE MAP IS STILL WORTH DECLARING. Nothing to compare today, but it records where the layout lives so a second copy gets added to the group rather than drifting quietly beside it.

cas-ccps:RubricQueue.why: The pair that would have caught the RQ05 drift. 05 writes the row; 34 deliberately derived its own indices from that writer's appendRow() call rather than trusting RQ05, and said so in a comment. Now the comparison is automatic.

cas-ccps:TeacherMatrix.why: Flow 1 writes this sheet and 37_FlowInputBuilder.js reads it by position, so a shift silently feeds Flow 2 the wrong field. 37's own header notes that FI_TM_COLUMNS_ is a redeclaration of TM08 under a different name, because the two live in different GAS projects with separate global scopes -- exactly the situation where drift is invisible.
cas-ccps:TeacherMatrix.authoritative: TM08 in 08_TeacherConfirmationStep.js, which that file's header calls the authoritative source

cas-ccps:WarmUpQueue.why: 21 columns indexed by hardcoded constants in three scripts, which is why 41_WarmUpFlowBridge.js added tabs instead of columns. Two prefixed constant runs and one object map describe the same sheet.
cas-ccps:WarmUpQueue.authoritative: WQ24_* in 24_WarmUpBridge.js, the script that writes the rows

cas-ccps:STAGING_PIPELINE.why: Flow 2's trigger queue. Declared with one map for now -- see _doctrine on why a single-map group is still worth declaring. NOT the same sheet as kos-personal's STAGING_PIPELINE below.
cas-ccps:STAGING_PIPELINE.authoritative: WD_STAGING_PIPELINE_COLUMNS in 34_QueueWatchdog.js, derived from the writer

cas-ccps:FlowInput.why: Flow 2's materialized input row. One map, and it should stay that way: 39_FlowFixtures.js and 42_FlowBuildSpec.js both READ FI rather than redeclaring it, which is the pattern this whole file exists to encourage.

leader-hub:AI_Queue.why: The Flow writes Status and Result here by position, so drift breaks reading AND writing. leader-hub/FlowOps.gs's checkAiQueueSchema verifies the live header row against this map at runtime; this checks the map itself has not been copied.
leader-hub:AI_Queue.authoritative: AIQ_COL in leader-hub/EmailBridge.gs, beside the AI_QUEUE_HEADERS it indexes

kos-personal:STUDIO_RETURN.why: Where a Workspace Flow writes its raw output for the harvest. A different sheet from cas-ccps's WarmUpFlowReturn despite the same role.

leader-hub:ai-flows._note: No materialize role: the client submits a whole payload as one JSON string, so there is nothing to flatten. queueAiJob_ is the write path.

kos-personal:studio-flows._note: No materialize role: the payload already lives in a Drive Doc that a native step reads directly.
